title: Container Bookings: amount and entries of the change-of-destination fee
content:
## Rule
Under the Container Bookings product line, the change-of-destination fee is the tier's per-container change-of-destination fee multiplied by the chargeable containers, one fee entry per change, whatever the free allowance, and the product is rounded to two decimal places only at the end. A fee is written only while a change is still owing one. Each fee entry carries, as its sailing, the sailing shown on the change-of-destination amendment entry it charges, which is the sailing the booking was allocated when the change was logged. The change still counts toward the free amendment allowance.

## Calculation order
1. Take the tier's per-container change-of-destination fee.
2. Multiply it by the chargeable containers.
3. Round the product to two decimal places, once, at the end.
4. Write one entry for each change still owing a fee, carrying the sailing shown on that change's amendment entry.

## Worked example (hypothetical)
*Hypothetical per-container fee of 275.00 and 7 chargeable containers, for illustration only:* 275.00 multiplied by 7 is 1925.00, booked as one entry for the change. If two changes were still owing, two entries of 1925.00 would be written, one per change.

## Wrong reading and correct basis
| Wrong reading | Correct basis |
|---|---|
| The fee is waived while the booking still has free amendments. | The fee is due whatever the free allowance; the change still uses up one amendment of the allowance. |
| The entry takes the sailing the booking is on today. | The entry takes the sailing shown on the amendment entry of the change, the sailing allocated when the change was logged. |
| Two owing changes are combined into one entry. | One entry is written per change. |
